Author: 9meia9meia9meia
Description:
[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/45572/45572-1778553036-1046900099.png[/img][/center]

[center][size=4][b]PowerGrid[/b][/size][/center]

PowerGrid adds a lightweight power system to Stardew Valley: generators, batteries, cables, conduits, fuels, powered artisan machines, and a new industrial processing tier.

Build power networks, connect locations, store EU, and use the Power Tab to monitor supply, demand, storage, machine status, generators, batteries, and conduits.

EU means Energy Units. PowerGrid uses EU for generated power, cable throughput, battery storage, and machine demand. PowerGrid updates once every Stardew 10-minute time tick, so EU/tick can be read as EU per 10 in-game minutes.

Power does not duplicate items or change machine outputs. Powered machines simply work faster, so the mod is meant to add infrastructure planning and progression without replacing Stardew's core production loop.

[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/45572/45572-1778553104-675344325.gif[/img][/center]

[size=4][b]Current release status[/b][/size]

PowerGrid 0.3.1 is the current public feedback release. The mod is playable and has been tested in real saves, but balance and compatibility may still change while the system matures.

Version 0.3.1 expands PowerGrid into industrial processing with Electric Smelter, Industrial Recycler, Powered Dehydrator, six machine upgrades, a new machine panel for upgrade handling, refreshed sprites, updated bundled player guides, and finalized Spanish localization for the new 0.3 content.

Version 0.2.1 was a maintenance release focused on mod-author API safety and documentation. It added API version discovery, safer custom machine registration, and an included API.md guide for mod authors who want to integrate their own machines with PowerGrid.

Community feedback is especially important at this stage. Reports about balance, confusing UI, compatibility issues, weird edge cases, or progression pacing are very welcome.

[size=4][b]Main features[/b][/size]

[list]
[*]Steam, wind, combustion, and radioisotope generators.[/*]
[*]Basic and iridium power batteries.[/*]
[*]Copper, iron, iridium, and energized iridium cables with different throughput limits.[/*]
[*]Power conduits for linking networks between locations.[/*]
[*]Power Tab UI for viewing networks, machines, generators, batteries, and conduits. Open it with [b]P[/b] or [b]K[/b].[/*]

[/list][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/45572/45572-1778553062-2132756487.png[/img]

[size=4][b]How power works[/b][/size]

Generators produce EU. EU means Energy Units, PowerGrid's internal unit for generated, stored, moved, and consumed power. Batteries store EU. Cables and conduits connect machines into networks. Powered machines consume EU while working and receive a speed bonus.

PowerGrid simulates power once every Stardew 10-minute time tick. In older guide text or technical API docs, you may see this written as EU/tick. For normal play, you can read that as EU per 10 in-game minutes.

If a network does not have enough power, most machines still behave normally while unpowered. PowerGrid is designed to enhance production setups, not punish normal Stardew gameplay. Electric Smelter is the main exception: it needs a live powered network to start smelting.

Batteries store surplus EU and keep their stored charge when picked up and placed somewhere else. By default, batteries leak a small amount of stored energy each morning.

[size=4][b]Progression path[/b][/size]

PowerGrid recipes unlock in bundles as your farm progresses. By default, the mod checks your existing progress and grants recipes automatically.

[list]
[*][b]Grid Starter[/b] unlocks at [b]Mining 5[/b] or when you know the [b]Lightning Rod[/b] recipe. Includes Copper Cable, Steam Generator, and Basic Power Battery.[/*]
[*][b]Powered Artisan[/b] unlocks when you know the [b]Preserves Jar[/b] or [b]Keg[/b] recipe. Includes Industrial Preserves Jar and Metal Keg.[/*]
[*][b]Fuel Tech[/b] unlocks at [b]Mining 7[/b] and when you know the [b]Lightning Rod[/b] recipe. Includes Biofuel, Iron Cable, Combustion Generator, Electric Smelter, Heating Coil, Efficiency Core, Catalyst Chamber, Industrial Recycler, Sorting Magnet, Powered Dehydrator, Drying Rack Array, and Heat Regulator.[/*]
[*][b]Advanced Grid[/b] unlocks at [b]Mining 9[/b] and when you know the [b]Lightning Rod[/b] recipe. Includes Iridium Cable, Wind Generator, Iridium Power Battery, Power Conduit, Metal Cask, and Hard Iridium Keg.[/*]
[*][b]High Density Grid[/b] unlocks at [b]Mining 10[/b], when you know the [b]Lightning Rod[/b] recipe, when you know the [b]Solar Panel[/b] recipe, and when you know the [b]Iridium Power Battery[/b] recipe. Includes Energized Iridium Cable, Radioisotope Fuel, and Radioisotope Generator.[/*]
[/list]The intended flow is to start with a small steam-powered setup, move into stronger biofuel power and better cables, expand into larger multi-location networks with conduits, build into industrial processing with upgrades, and then finish with high-density late-game networks around radioisotope power.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/45572/45572-1777929082-21597002.png[/img]

[size=4][b]Design goals[/b][/size]

[list]
[*]Add infrastructure planning without turning Stardew into a factory game.[/*]
[*]Make powered production feel useful, but not mandatory.[/*]
[*]Keep normal machines and vanilla production relevant.[/*]
[*]Support bigger artisan setups without making them free or instant.[/*]
[*]Give players a clearer reason to build dedicated utility spaces, sheds, and power rooms.[/*]
[/list][size=4][b]Important notes[/b][/size]

[list]
[*]Open the Power Tab with [b]P[/b] or [b]K[/b] to inspect networks, machines, generators, batteries, and conduits.[/*]
[*]EU means Energy Units. PowerGrid uses EU for generation, cable throughput, battery storage, and machine demand.[/*]
[*]PowerGrid updates once per Stardew 10-minute time tick, so EU/tick means EU per 10 in-game minutes.[/*]
[*]Wind Generators only produce EU outdoors.[/*]
[*]Steam Generators use Coal, Wood, or Hardwood.[/*]
[*]Combustion Generators use Biofuel.[/*]
[*]Radioisotope Generators use Radioisotope Fuel or Radioactive Bars.[/*]
[*]Radioisotope Fuel is much more efficient than using raw Radioactive Bars.[/*]
[*]Power Conduits link networks between locations.[/*]
[*]Electric Smelter needs a powered network to begin smelting.[/*]
[*]Industrial Recycler and Powered Dehydrator still work without power, but PowerGrid speeds them up when EU is available.[/*]
[*]Open the new industrial machine panel with [b]Shift + right-click[/b] on Electric Smelter, Industrial Recycler, or Powered Dehydrator to install or remove upgrades.[/*]
[*]Batteries keep their stored EU when picked up and placed somewhere else.[/*]
[*]The download includes short player guides inside the mod folder: PLAYER_GUIDE.md in English, GUIA_DO_JOGADOR.pt-BR.md in Brazilian Portuguese, and GUIA_DEL_JUGADOR.es.md in Spanish.[/*]
[*]PowerGrid packages are distributed through Nexus. GitHub is source-only.[/*]
[/list][size=4][b]Requirements[/b][/size]

[list]
[*]Stardew Valley 1.6+[/*]
[*]SMAPI 4.0.0+[/*]
[/list][size=4][b]Strongly recommended mods[/b][/size]

PowerGrid can be played by itself, but it is designed to feel much better in a larger production-focused setup.

[list]
[*][b]Grapes of Ferngill[/b] - strongly recommended. Hard Iridium Keg is designed around Grapes of Ferngill's Hardwood Keg behavior. Without Grapes of Ferngill, Hard Iridium Keg falls back to vanilla Keg behavior.[/*]
[*][b]Automate[/b] or [b]Event Driven Automation[/b] - strongly recommended for larger power networks. PowerGrid adds more production infrastructure, and automation makes large machine rooms much more comfortable to run.[/*]
[/list][size=4][b]Optional compatibility[/b][/size]

[list]
[*]Generic Mod Config Menu - in-game configuration.[/*]
[*]UI Info Suite - tooltip/status integration for PowerGrid machines.[/*]
[*]Automate - chest-based machine logistics.[/*]
[*]Event Driven Automation - event-driven automation support.[/*]
[*]Grapes of Ferngill - enables Hard Iridium Keg to use Hardwood Keg behavior. Without it, Hard Iridium Keg falls back to vanilla Keg behavior.[/*]
[/list]Note that Automate and Event Driven Automation are not compatible with each other.

[size=4][b]Mod author API[/b][/size]

PowerGrid 0.3.1 still includes API version 1, a public SMAPI API for registering compatible custom machine consumers.

For a simple integration, another mod only needs to retrieve PowerGrid's API and call RegisterConsumer for its machine's qualified item ID. If that machine uses normal Stardew object processing, PowerGrid can detect it, show it in the Machines tab, allocate EU while it works, and apply the configured speed bonus.

The download includes API.md with the current integration contract, a minimum working example, common mistakes, and a verification checklist.

[size=4][b]Installation[/b][/size]

[list=1]
[*]Install SMAPI.[/*]
[*]Download PowerGrid from this page.[/*]
[*]Extract the folder into your Stardew Valley [b]Mods[/b] folder.[/*]
[*]The installed folder should look like [b]Stardew Valley/Mods/[SMAPI] PowerGrid/manifest.json[/b].[/*]
[*]Launch the game through SMAPI.[/*]
[/list]For testing on an existing modded save, I strongly recommend using a backup or a test save first. If you use Cinderleaf's sandbox setup, that is a great place to test before adding it to a long-running save.

[size=4][b]Translations[/b][/size]

PowerGrid currently includes English, Brazilian Portuguese, and Spanish.

Spanish translation and guide by [b]Hayato2236[/b].

Please do not publish translations as separate mod pages.

If you want to translate PowerGrid, please reach out so we can collaborate and keep translations in one official source of truth for the mod and its versions. That makes updates easier for everyone and avoids players downloading outdated translation packs.

[size=4][b]Sprite collaboration[/b][/size]

Special thanks to [b]ErraticPixel[/b] for the idea and first sprite prototypes for the new keg sprites. I refined the final keg sprites visually, with palette inspiration from the earthy visual style of [b]DaisyNiko's mods[/b] and [b]Gwen's Craftables[/b] by [b]Gweniaczek[/b].

Sprites are my weak point. If any member of the community would like to help improve existing sprites or create sprites for future generators, machines, batteries, fuels, upgrades, or other PowerGrid content, you are very welcome to reach out.

I would love for visual improvements to happen collaboratively and consistently with the mod's direction.

[size=4][b]Feedback wanted[/b][/size]

Since PowerGrid is still an early public mod, feedback is extremely valuable.

Helpful feedback includes:

[list]
[*]Balance thoughts: recipes, fuel usage, power output, machine speed, progression, and upgrades.[/*]
[*]Power Tab readability or missing information.[/*]
[*]Machine Panel readability or upgrade flow issues.[/*]
[*]Compatibility issues with other mods.[/*]
[*]Automation edge cases.[/*]
[*]Sprite or visual clarity suggestions.[/*]
[*]Bugs with sleeping, machine timers, conduits, batteries, generators, or industrial machines.[/*]
[/list]Please include your SMAPI log when reporting bugs, especially if other mods are involved.

[size=4][b]Known direction[/b][/size]

PowerGrid is intended to grow into a progression-focused power and production system with clearer early, mid, and late-game infrastructure. Future updates may continue expanding generator tiers, upgrade items, fuels, machine polish, UI polish, and compatibility.

Thank you for testing PowerGrid and helping shape where the mod goes next.
